proof:
PROOF OF `HausdorffDensityBounds` (Simon, Ch. 1, (2.4)–(2.6) and Theorem 3.26; printed proofs, transcribed and completed).

Statement. Let (X, d) be a metric space, n ≥ 0 real, and A ⊆ X an Hⁿ-measurable set.
 (1) If Hⁿ(A) < ∞, then Θ^{*n}(Hⁿ, A, x) ≤ 1 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A.
 (2) If Hⁿ_δ(A) < ∞ for every real δ > 0, then Θ^{*n}(Hⁿ_∞, A, x) ≥ 2^{−n} for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A.

Conventions. For δ ∈ (0, ∞], Hⁿ_δ(∅) = 0 and, for nonempty E, Hⁿ_δ(E) = ω_n inf{Σ_j (diam C_j/2)ⁿ : E ⊆ ⋃_j C_j countable, diam C_j < δ} (2.2) (empty C_j contribute 0; inf ∅ = ∞; ω_n = π^{n/2}/Γ(n/2+1) > 0; x⁰ = 1). Hⁿ_δ is an outer measure, non-increasing in δ, Hⁿ_∞ ≤ Hⁿ_δ, and Hⁿ = sup_{δ>0} Hⁿ_δ = lim_{δ↓0} Hⁿ_δ (2.1) (including δ = ∞ in the supremum changes nothing). Θ^{*n}(σ, A, x) := limsup_{ρ↓0} σ(A ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρⁿ) (3.1), B_ρ(x) the closed ball. “P for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A” means Hⁿ({x ∈ A : not P(x)}) = 0.

Dependencies. Theorem 1.13 = sibling `caratheodory_criterion`; Theorem 1.15 = sibling `borel_regular_approximation`; Theorem 3.3 = first conjunct of sibling `upper_density_comparison_and_theorem`.

STEP 1 ((2.4), (2.5)). If E, F ⊆ X and r > 0 with d(e, f) ≥ r for all e ∈ E, f ∈ F, then Hⁿ_δ(E ∪ F) = Hⁿ_δ(E) + Hⁿ_δ(F) for every δ ∈ (0, r], hence Hⁿ(E ∪ F) = Hⁿ(E) + Hⁿ(F).
 Proof. “≤” is subadditivity. For “≥” we may assume Hⁿ_δ(E ∪ F) < ∞. Let {C_j} be a countable cover of E ∪ F with diam C_j < δ ≤ r. No C_j meets both E and F. The C_j meeting E cover E and the C_j meeting F cover F, with disjoint sets of indices, so ω_nΣ_j(diam C_j/2)ⁿ ≥ Hⁿ_δ(E) + Hⁿ_δ(F). Take the infimum over covers; then let δ ↓ 0.

STEP 2 ((2.6): Hⁿ is Borel regular).
 (a) By Step 1 and Carathéodory's criterion (sibling `caratheodory_criterion`, applied to the outer measure Hⁿ on X), every Borel set is Hⁿ-measurable.
 (b) Borel hulls (using Remark 2.3(1): diam C̄ = diam C, so in (2.2) the C_j may be taken closed). Let E ⊆ X. If Hⁿ(E) = ∞ take X. Otherwise, for each k ≥ 1, Hⁿ_{1/k}(E) ≤ Hⁿ(E) < ∞, so there is a countable cover {C_{kj}}_j of E by closed sets with diam C_{kj} < 1/k and ω_nΣ_j(diam C_{kj}/2)ⁿ < Hⁿ_{1/k}(E) + 1/k. G := ⋂_k ⋃_j C_{kj} is Borel and contains E. For m ≤ k, Hⁿ_{1/m}(G) ≤ Hⁿ_{1/k}(G) ≤ ω_nΣ_j(diam C_{kj}/2)ⁿ < Hⁿ_{1/k}(E) + 1/k ≤ Hⁿ(E) + 1/k; letting k → ∞ and then m → ∞, Hⁿ(G) ≤ Hⁿ(E); the reverse inequality is monotonicity.

STEP 3 (remarks after (1.12)). If A is Hⁿ-measurable with Hⁿ(A) < ∞, then σ := Hⁿ⌞A (σ(S) = Hⁿ(A ∩ S)) is Borel regular and finite. [Hⁿ-measurable sets are σ-measurable: σ(S) = Hⁿ(S∩A∩E) + Hⁿ((S∩A)∖E). Hulls: by Step 2 take Borel B₁ ⊇ A with Hⁿ(B₁) = Hⁿ(A), so Hⁿ(B₁ ∖ A) = 0, and Borel B₂ ⊇ B₁ ∖ A with Hⁿ(B₂) = 0; for S take Borel B₃ ⊇ S ∩ A with Hⁿ(B₃) = Hⁿ(S ∩ A); B := B₃ ∪ (X ∖ B₁) ∪ B₂ ⊇ S is Borel and σ(B) ≤ Hⁿ(B₃) + Hⁿ(A ∖ B₁) + Hⁿ(B₂) = σ(S).] Being finite, σ is open σ-finite (V_n := X); and in a metric space every closed set C (C ≠ ∅) is ⋂_k {x : dist(x, C) < 1/k}, a countable intersection of open sets.

STEP 4 (proof of (1); printed). Assume Hⁿ(A) < ∞; σ := Hⁿ⌞A as in Step 3. Let t > 1, ε > 0, and A_t := {x ∈ A : Θ^{*n}(Hⁿ, A, x) ≥ t}. By Theorem 1.15(1) (sibling) for σ, σ(A_t) = inf{σ(U) : U ⊇ A_t open}, so there is an open U ⊇ A_t with Hⁿ(A ∩ U) = σ(U) < σ(A_t) + ε = Hⁿ(A_t) + ε. For x ∈ A_t ⊆ U we have B_ρ(x) ⊆ U for small ρ, so σ((A ∩ U) ∩ B_ρ(x)) = Hⁿ(A ∩ B_ρ(x)) for small ρ and Θ^{*n}(σ, A ∩ U, x) = Θ^{*n}(Hⁿ, A, x) ≥ t. Theorem 3.3 (sibling) applied to the Borel regular σ with A₁ := A_t ⊆ A₂ := A ∩ U gives
  t·Hⁿ(A_t) ≤ σ(A ∩ U) = Hⁿ(A ∩ U) < Hⁿ(A_t) + ε.
Letting ε → 0, t·Hⁿ(A_t) ≤ Hⁿ(A_t) ≤ Hⁿ(A) < ∞, so Hⁿ(A_t) = 0 since t > 1. Finally {x ∈ A : Θ^{*n}(Hⁿ, A, x) > 1} = ⋃_k A_{1+1/k} is Hⁿ-null, which is (1).

STEP 5 (proof of (2)). The printed argument is completed below; the measurability of A is not needed. Write Θ_∞(x) := Θ^{*n}(Hⁿ_∞, A, x).
 5.0 (n = 0.) For x ∈ A and ρ > 0 the set A ∩ B_ρ(x) contains x, so every cover of it contains a nonempty set, which costs (diam/2)⁰ = 1; hence H⁰_∞(A ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≥ ω_0 = 1 = ω_0ρ⁰ and Θ_∞(x) ≥ 1 = 2^{−0} for every x ∈ A. From now on n > 0.
 5.1 (Lemma.) If E ⊆ X and diam E < δ < ∞, then Hⁿ_δ(E) = Hⁿ_∞(E). [Hⁿ_∞ ≤ Hⁿ_δ always. Conversely, if {D_i} is a cover of E admissible for Hⁿ_∞, then {D_i ∩ E} covers E, diam(D_i ∩ E) ≤ min(diam D_i, diam E) < δ, and its cost is not larger.]
 5.2 For j ≥ 1 let B_j := {x ∈ A : Hⁿ_∞(A ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ (1 − 1/j)2^{−n}ω_nρⁿ for all ρ ∈ (0, 1/j)}. If x ∈ A and Θ_∞(x) < 2^{−n}, pick c with Θ_∞(x) < c < 2^{−n}; then Hⁿ_∞(A ∩ B_ρ(x)) < cω_nρⁿ for all ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀) for some ρ₀ > 0, and choosing j with 1/j ≤ ρ₀ and (1 − 1/j)2^{−n} ≥ c gives x ∈ B_j. (This is the printed choice of δ_x ∈ (0, 1) and of B ⊆ B₀ with δ_x > 1/j.) So {x ∈ A : Θ_∞(x) < 2^{−n}} ⊆ ⋃_j B_j, and it suffices to prove Hⁿ(B_j) = 0 for each j.
 5.3 Fix j, put δ := 1/j and B := B_j, and let δ' ∈ (0, δ]. Let {C_i} be any countable cover of B with diam C_i < δ'; discarding the C_i that miss B (this lowers the cost and keeps a cover) we may assume C_i ∩ B ≠ ∅; pick x_i ∈ C_i ∩ B and let r_i := diam C_i < δ'. Every point of C_i is within r_i of x_i, and B ⊆ A, so B ∩ C_i ⊆ A ∩ B_{r_i}(x_i).
  • If r_i > 0: diam(B ∩ C_i) ≤ r_i < δ', so by 5.1 and the definition of B (x_i ∈ B, 0 < r_i < δ' ≤ δ),
    Hⁿ_{δ'}(B ∩ C_i) = Hⁿ_∞(B ∩ C_i) ≤ Hⁿ_∞(A ∩ B_{r_i}(x_i)) ≤ (1 − δ)2^{−n}ω_n r_iⁿ = (1 − δ)ω_n(diam C_i/2)ⁿ.
  • If r_i = 0: B ∩ C_i = {x_i}, and Hⁿ_{δ'}({x_i}) = 0 = (1 − δ)ω_n(diam C_i/2)ⁿ (the one-point cover costs ω_n0ⁿ = 0 as n > 0).
  Hence Hⁿ_{δ'}(B) ≤ Σ_i Hⁿ_{δ'}(B ∩ C_i) ≤ (1 − δ)ω_nΣ_i(diam C_i/2)ⁿ. Taking the infimum over all such covers, Hⁿ_{δ'}(B) ≤ (1 − δ)Hⁿ_{δ'}(B). Since Hⁿ_{δ'}(B) ≤ Hⁿ_{δ'}(A) < ∞ by hypothesis and 1 − δ < 1, Hⁿ_{δ'}(B) = 0. As δ' ∈ (0, δ] was arbitrary, Hⁿ(B) = sup_{0<δ'≤δ}Hⁿ_{δ'}(B) = 0.
 (This is the printed contradiction argument “we conclude from (1), (2) that Hⁿ_δ(B) = 0, hence Hⁿ(B) = 0”, with two corrections: the printed bound (1) is stated only for ρ < δ/2 but is used at radius 2ρ_j = diam C_j < δ, so here the density bound is recorded for all ρ < δ via the definition of B_j and the lemma 5.1 for sets of diameter < δ; and the passage to Hⁿ uses all scales δ' ≤ δ. The step marked “XXX” in the source is thereby completed.)
 5.4 Hence {x ∈ A : Θ_∞(x) < 2^{−n}} is Hⁿ-null, i.e. 2^{−n} ≤ Θ^{*n}(Hⁿ_∞, A, x) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A. In Lean, 2^{−n} is `(2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ (-n)`, Hⁿ_∞ is `simonHausdorffContentOuter n ∞`, and the hypothesis is `simonHausdorffContent n (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A < ∞` for every real δ > 0. ∎

Formalization note (non-binding): `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_26_i` (Chapter01/HausdorffDensityBounds.lean) and `simon_theorem_3_26_ii` (Chapter01/HausdorffContentDensity.lean) give (1) and (2) in null-set form, Hⁿ{x | x ∈ A ∧ 1 < Θ} = 0 and Hⁿ{x | x ∈ A ∧ Θ_∞ < 2^{−n}} = 0; convert with `ae_iff`, `not_imp`, `not_le`. `simonHausdorffContent` unfolds to `simonHausdorffContentOuter`.
key_steps: (2.4)/(2.5): Hⁿ_δ and Hⁿ are additive on positively separated sets; by the Carathéodory criterion every Borel set is Hⁿ-measurable.
Borel hulls from closed covers make Hⁿ Borel regular; hence Hⁿ⌞A is Borel regular and finite.
(1): outer regularity (1.15(1)) for Hⁿ⌞A and Theorem 3.3 give t·Hⁿ(A_t) ≤ Hⁿ(A_t) + ε, so Hⁿ(A_t) = 0 for t > 1.
(2): n = 0 is immediate; for n > 0, Hⁿ_δ = Hⁿ_∞ on sets of diameter < δ.
The sets B_j, where Hⁿ_∞(A ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ (1 − 1/j)2^{−n}ω_nρⁿ for ρ < 1/j, exhaust {x ∈ A : Θ_∞(x) < 2^{−n}}.
Covering B_j by sets of diameter < δ' ≤ 1/j gives Hⁿ_{δ'}(B_j) ≤ (1 − 1/j)Hⁿ_{δ'}(B_j) < ∞, so Hⁿ(B_j) = 0 (correcting the printed factor-2 slip).
